title: Laetoli footprints
summary: At Laetoli in northern Tanzania, hominin tracks pressed into volcanic ash some 3.66 million years ago are the oldest known hominin footprints. Mary Leakey and co-workers found them in 1976 and excavation was complete by 1978; the makers are most likely Australopithecus afarensis. A second set, reported in 2016 at Site S, was left by two individuals.

uncertainty.note: Converted as year = 1950 minus age. Both opened pages give 3.66 million years with no error range.

reviewer_note: Pin is derived: the eLife paper puts Laetoli about 50 km south of Olduvai Gorge, and I offset the OSM Olduvai point by that distance, hence 40 km uncertainty. No opened page gives Laetoli coordinates. Discovery year conflicts: Archaeology and the eLife Insight say 1976 (excavated by 1978); the eLife paper says discovered in 1978. The Site G attribution to A. afarensis is called controversial in the paper.
